revision: V3.1: adds the enumerable enclave roster index (get_enclave_count, get_enclave_by_index), the cancel_proposal bounded-liveness path, a claim_payout fund-safety guard, and bytes/str telemetry-body resilience.

verification.method: live view reads via genlayer-js / genlayer-py at the current head
verification.note: GenVM is not an EVM chain, so eth_getCode returns 0x even for a live contract and cannot be used to compare deployed bytecode against source. Deployment is instead evidenced by live view reads answering from this address. The source hash above is the repository revision this record was written against. That the roster index is genuinely part of the deployed revision is established behaviourally: get_enclave_count answers on this address (a method that did not exist on the predecessor), and get_enclave_by_index(0) reverts out-of-range on the empty roster exactly as the guard specifies.

observed_at_deploy.get_enclave_by_index(0): reverts ERR_INVALID_STATE (index out of range) -- correct for an empty roster

state_note: This address is freshly deployed and EMPTY: no enclaves, no treaties, next_treaty_id 1. The board therefore reads ON-CHAIN / EMPTY until the protocol is populated. To reproduce the demo state, run the autonomous duet and then the wider roster against this address (agent/chain.py already points here): `.venv/bin/python -m agent.demo` (found -> propose -> reject -> adapt -> ratify -> dispute -> verdict), then `.venv/bin/python -m agent.seed` (founds Vantage, Aegis, Quorum, Solstice and wires the star + mesh). With the V3.1 roster index the frontend now lists every founded enclave directly via get_enclave_count + get_enclave_by_index, so agents are visible even before they join a treaty. Both studio-next.genlayer.com and studio-dev.genlayer.com serve chain 61997 and answer identically; the repository standardises on studio-next, matching the hackathon brief.
